input: # Two paren operators share the opener `(`: a group, `paren`, whose
# preval is inactive, and a call, `call`, whose preval is active. A value
# before the opener selects the call, and no value the group. The
# runner's evaluator writes each operation as [op.name, ...terms], so a
# cell names the operator that built each node, which the operators'
# common source `(` cannot show. Only the last operator declared on an
# opener used to be active: with `call` last a group read as a call
# (`(e)` and `e()` were both a call of `e`), and with `paren` last `f(x)`
# was no call at all. The default `plain` gives way to the table's own
# group on `(` and `)`. The runners also parse every row with the two
# operators declared in the other order, which must not matter.
